title: Science Topical summary (WATER)
text:
PRIMARY SCIENCE
 TOPICAL REVISION
 WATER
 SUMMARIZED SCIENCE REVISION NOTES
 WATER
 WATER IS USED:-
 a) in the home
 b) on the farm
 c) for recreation
 d) in industries
 e) for transport
 WATER USES AT HOME
 a) For drinking
 b) For cooking
 c) For washing e.g. clothes, bodies, utensils
 d) For cleaning the house, toilets, latrines, etc.
 e) Building houses
 f) For putting out fires
 N.B. Water for drinking is made safe by boiling.
 WATER USES ON THE FARM
 - Watering plants
 - Watering animals
 - Mixing farm chemicals
 - Rearing fish in a fish pond
 - Washing farm tools
 N.B. Supplying water to plants during the dry season is called irrigation.
 USES OF WATER IN RECREATION
 Recreation is doing an activity for enjoyment, a way of spending free time.
 Water sports include:
 - Swimming
 - Boat racing /rowing
 - Surfing
 - Fishing for fun
 - Water polo
 - Water skiing etc.
 USES OF WATER IN INDUSTRIES
 - Used for cleaning/washing e.g. coffee berries, fruits
 - Processing raw materials
 - Used for beautifying the environment e.g. A fountain – a decorative
 structure that produces a steam of water that rises into the air.
 - Used to make drinks e.g. soft drinks
 - For cooling machines
 - Putting out fires
 USES OF WATER IN TRANSPORTATION
 Boats, ships, canoes, oil tankers or ferries can be used to transport people
 or goods from one place to another.
 STORING WATER
 Water can be stored in:
 a) Pots
 b) Tanks
 c) Buckets
 d) Jerry cans
 e) Dams – store huge amounts of water
 N.B. The easiest and fastest way of transporting water is by the use of pipes.
 We store water for future use.
 WATER-BORNE DISEASES
 • Water-borne diseases are diseases that are transmitted through
 water.
 • Water that contains germs is said to be contaminated.
 Examples of water-borne diseases
 • Cholera
 • Typhoid
 • Bilharzia
 Cholera
 • Cholera is caused by a bacteria germ found in contaminated water
 used for drinking.
 • Water can be contaminated by human faeces especially where there
 are floods.
 • Flies also carry cholera germs to food.
 Signs and symptoms of cholera
 -Severe abdominal pains
 -Vomiting
 -Violent diarrhea with mucus, hence the name “rice-water”
 -Dehydration due to loss of large amounts of fluids through vomiting and
 diarrhoea
 -Death can occur within a day if care is NOT taken
 Prevention of cholera
 • Use of pit latrines or toilets to dispose of faeces and urine
 • Keeping latrines/toilets clean to keep away houseflies
 • Washing hands with soap after visiting the toilet or before
 preparing or taking meals.
 • Washing foods eaten raw before eating i.e. fruits and
 vegetables
 • Boiling or treating water for domestic use to kill germs
 • Keeping water sources free from contamination i.e. avoid:
 • Urinating in them
 • Passing out faeces
 • Bathing/washing clothes or utensils in water sources
 • Watering animals around the sources
 • Wearing protective clothing such as rubber gloves and
 gumboots when handling stagnant water (might be
 contaminated)
 • Infected people should be taken for medical help to avoid
 the spread of cholera.
 Typhoid
 • Caused by a bacteria
 • Typhoid fever affects the intestines
 • Spread when one eats food or drinks water that is contaminated with
 faeces and urine from an infected person.
 Signs and symptoms of Typhoid
 Fever i.e. higher body temperature than normal
 Abdominal pains
 Skin rashes
 Aches in the muscles and joints
 Sores or ulcers on the walls of the intestines which may result in bleeding
 Severe headache
 Prevention of Typhoid fever
 • Drinking boiled or treated water
 • Washing raw foods (fruits and vegetables) thoroughly
 before eating or cooking them
 • Using latrines and toilets properly to pass out faeces and
 urine
 • Keep toilets and latrines clean
 • Boil water for cleaning and rinsing utensils, especially in
 areas prone to typhoid outbreaks
 • Wash hands with soap before eating, handling food or after
 visiting the toilet
 • People handling food in hotels, schools, hospitals and
 restaurants to go for a regular typhoid check-up.
 Bilharzia
 • Bilharzia is caused by a parasite called fluke (bilharzia
 worms)
 • Flukes live in the blood vessels of the abdomen of a human
 being
 • A person normally passes out the eggs of bilharzia flukes in
 the urine or faeces
 • Eggs are passed into water and they hatch into larvae
 • The larvae enter the body of a fresh-water snail and
 develop further.
 • After some time, the larvae leave the body of the water
 snail and get into the water ready to attack human beings.
 • If one walks bare-footed, swims, bathes or drinks
 contaminated water, the larvae enter the body.
 • The larvae penetrate the body through the skin particularly
 the legs.
 N.B. - There are two types of bilharzia-causing worms.
 - One type affects the bladder while the other affects the
 intestines.
 Signs and symptoms
 • Blood in the urine and stool (faeces)
 • Fever develops about four weeks after infection
 • “Swimmers itch”. This is severe itching of the bowels and
 the bladder.
 • Coughing
 • Diarrhoea
 • Skin rash if the flukes are many
 Prevention of Bilharzia
 • Wear protective clothing such as gumboots and rubber
 gloves when walking through or working in pools of water
 e.g. rice fields
 • Kill water snails using chemicals
 • Always use a latrine or a toilet to pass out stool or urine to
 avoid contaminating water bodies.
 • If not needed, drain stagnant water that might harbour
 snails
 • Boil drinking water always
 • Observe cleanliness at all times
 N.B. Boiling drinking water kills all the disease-causing germs.
 MAKINI SCHOOL
 WATER POLLUTION
 WATER POLLUTION
 1. Water pollution is making water impure or contaminating it.
 2. Polluted water is not safe for drinking by animals and human
 beings or for watering crops.
 WAYS IN WHICH WATER IS POLLUTED
 a) Human and animal waste.
 When human beings and animals pass their waste into water sources, many
 bacteria and viruses grow and pollute the water.
 The bacteria may cause water-borne diseases and make the water unsafe for
 drinking.
 b) Oil spillage
 Oil tankers transporting crude oil may have accidents in seas or lake-shores
 and spill oil into the water.
 Oil spillage reduces the amount of oxygen in water which may lead to the
 suffocation of water animals.
 The animals that live in the sea shells die due to lack of oxygen which is
 brought about by the oil spillage.
 c) Industrial waste
 Factories and Industries built along sources of water may release untreated
 waste material into water thus polluting it. This makes it unfit for use.
 d) Uncontrolled use of farm chemicals
 Fertilizers and pesticides used in excess by farmers cause water pollution.
 The chemicals in pesticides and fertilizers are harmful.
 e) Floods
 When it rains, water becomes muddy and has solid impurities.
 f) Acid Rain
 Industries emit carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide in large amounts. When it
 rains these gases dissolve in water forming acid rain. Acid rain destroys iron
 sheets and kills water animals as well as destroying plants.
 EFFECTS OF WATER POLLUTION ON PLANTS
 1. Oil spills block plant roots affecting the absorption rate of roots.
 2. Water that contains excessive fertilizers, pesticides or herbicides can
 cause plants to dry.
 3. Oil spills also prevent sunlight from reaching water plants, hence they
 cannot make their own food.
 EFFECTS OF WATER POLLUTION ON ANIMALS
 1. Chemicals in polluted water may be poisonous to animals and can lead
 to death.
 2. Oil spills affect fish and other aquatic animals leading to death.
 3. Polluted water leads to water-borne diseases because it carries germs
 and internal parasites.
 EFFECTS OF WATER POLLUTION ON SOIL
 1. Acid rain makes the soil acidic, thus it cannot support the growth of
 plants.
 2. Some chemicals in water affect the fertility of the soil making it
 unfertile.
 3. Water pollution leads to poor aeration of the soil. This may lead to the
 death of soil, animals and plants.
 WAYS OF CONTROLLING WATER POLLUTION
 1. Practising proper hygiene
 2. Practising farming methods that reduce soil erosion
 3. Draw water for animals instead of taking them to water sources.
 4. Avoid dumping of industrial waste into water sources.
 5. Clearing accidental oil spills as soon as they happen.
 CONSERVATION OF WATER
 Conservation of water means the proper care and use of water and water
 sources. Conserving water ensures it’s spared for future use.
 WAYS OF CONSERVING WATER
 1. Harvesting
 2. Recycling
 3. Re-using
 4. Using water sparingly
 5. Mulching/shading
 6. Storing water in dams
 1. Harvesting water
 • Rain water can be collected and stored in tanks, trenches, drums, pots
 and dams.
 • The harvested water can be used for domestic purposes or watering
 animals.
 2. Recycling water
 Recycling water means treating water that has already been used so that it
 becomes suitable for use again e.g. sewage water can be recycled.
 3. Re-using water
 Water which has already been used can be used for another purpose. For
 example, water used to wash clothes can be used to flush the toilet.
 4. Using water sparingly
 • This is avoiding wastage of water and unnecessary usage of water.
 • When irrigating avoid overhead irrigation which uses a lot of
 water. Instead use drip irrigation.
 • Repair leaking taps and pipes
 5. Mulching/shading
 • A lot of water is lost through evaporation leaving plants with less water
 for growth.
 • Mulching or shading growing plants prevents too much evaporation.
 • In mulching, dry leaves and grass are spread at the root base of the
 plant.
 6. Storing water in dams
 • Dams and terraces are constructed to trap run-off water.
 • This water can be used for irrigation during the dry season.
 HARD AND SOFT WATER
 • Hard water is the water that does not form lather easily with soap
 because it contains large amounts of dissolved mineral salts e.g.
 magnesium, sodium and potassium.
 • Soft water is the water that lathers easily with soap because it
 does not contain dissolved mineral salts or contains little.
 • Dissolved salts in hard water react with soap to form a layer on
 the surface of water known as scum.
 • Natural pure water contains no mineral but as rain falls, water
 dissolves gases and dust particles present in the air.
 • When rain water penetrates the soil, it dissolves mineral salts
 present in the soil.
 • Some minerals cause temporary hardness while others cause
 permanent hardness of the water.
 • Sources of hard water include borehole, lake, sea, well.
 • Source of soft water includes rain water.
 HARD WATER
 Types of Hard Water
 • Temporary hardness
 • Permanent hardness
 Disadvantages of Hard Water
 1. Hard water wastes a lot of soap – A large quantity of soap is required
 before the water lathers. Time and energy is also wasted.
 2. Hard water stains clothes and discolours white clothes.
 The scum formed on the surface of water stains clothes and also
 discolours brightly coloured clothes.
 3. Hard water wears out clothes – Washing clothes with hard water
 requires vigorous rubbing to obtain lather. This makes them wear out
 easily.
 4. Hard water stains/discolours cooking utensils e.g. sufurias, kettles and
 water boilers. When used to boil hard water, mineral salts are
 deposited on the walls of the utensils as the water boils. The stains
 formed are called scale.
 5. Hard water wears out utensils due to the continuous rubbing of the
 utensils to remove the scale.
 6. Hard water clogs/blocks pipes – Minerals present in hard water react
 with the inside of the pipe to form scale that is deposited on the inside
 of the pipe. Scale forms a coat inside the pipe that
 leads to blockage.
 Note
 • Scale clogs the pipes of a water-heating system of a building
 making the water take a longer time to heat. This leads to
 wastage of heat.
 Softening hard water
 The process by which mineral salts are removed from hard water is called
 softening.
 Ways of softening hard water
 a) Boiling hard water
 b) Use of chemicals
 a) Boiling - is used to remove temporary hardness.
 When hard water is boiled, mineral salts present in the water break down and
 are deposited in the boiling container as scale.
 The water becomes soft.
 b) Use of chemicals – used to remove permanent hardness.
 Chemicals combine with the minerals in the water and drastically reduce the
 mineral content in the water.
